prompt.context: Your client is a PE firm that is considering buying one of two companies in the water filtration industry – DM or PM. There are two categories of products in the water filtration industry – POE (Point Of Entry) and POU (Point Of Use). Point of Entry systems are used outside the house or business – on pipes mostly. Point of Use systems are mostly inside the house or business – for example Brita, water coolers, etc.
prompt.question: The PE firm must decide which of the two companies – DM or PM – to purchase. The decision will be based on current revenue and potential growth. Which company should the PE firm acquire?

clarifying_info.q: What data is available to compare the two companies?
clarifying_info.a: Two exhibits are provided: Exhibit 1 shows the different types of filters and the market share of each company; Exhibit 2 shows the purchasing habits of consumers for each company.

clarifying_info.q: What are the revenue drivers for these companies?
clarifying_info.a: Each company sells filtration systems and replacement filters. You will need to work out the revenue from both streams.

exhibits.title: Product Types and Market Share
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of the water filtration market into Point of Entry (POE) and Point of Use (POU) product categories, with market share percentages for PM and DM in each sub-category. POE sub-categories: Filtration, Water Softeners, Non Salt Water Conditioners. POU sub-categories: Tap Filter, Faucet Mount, Pour Through, Plumbed-In, Plumbed-In to Separate Tap, Other.

exhibits.title: Consumer Purchasing Channels
exhibits.shows: Market share of PM, DM, and Other competitors across three retail channel types: Professional Stores, Branded Stores, and DIY Stores.

framework: Identify revenue streams for each company: system sales and filter sales
Calculate total revenue for DM and PM using provided data
Assess growth potential by comparing product mix (POE vs. POU), market share positions, and sales channel strength
Evaluate ease of market penetration, service offering, and pricing sensitivity for each
Synthesize findings into a recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate the total annual revenue for each of the two companies – DM and PM.
questions.guidance: Candidates should recognize two revenue streams: (1) sale of filtration systems and (2) recurring sale of replacement filters. The filter revenue stream is the key insight to surface. Revenue = (# systems sold x system price) + (# systems x # filters/year x filter price).

math.setup: Revenue = (units x unit price) for systems + (units x filters per year x filter price) for filters
steps: DM filter revenue: 3,000 systems x 1 filter/year x $100 = $300,000
PM filter revenue: 35,000 systems x 2 filters/year x $10 = $700,000
math.answer: DM total revenue = $3,300,000; PM total revenue = $4,200,000

questions.prompt: Which aspects would you look at in order to decide which of the two companies to purchase?
questions.guidance: Candidates should connect the revenue calculation to the strategic investment decision and compare the two companies across multiple dimensions. Strong answers cover: ease of market penetration, service offerings and aftermarket potential, ability to increase filter sales per system, price sensitivity of each customer base, marketing efforts required, and profitability (not just revenue). Using Exhibit 1 to assess POE vs. POU positioning and Exhibit 2 to assess channel strength should inform the analysis.

brainstorming.prompt: Which aspects would you look at in order to consider which of the two companies to purchase?

categories.name: Market Penetration
ideas: Ease of entering adjacent POE or POU segments
DM is concentrated in POE; PM has broader POU presence

categories.name: Revenue Quality
ideas: Recurring filter revenue as a percentage of total revenue
PM generates proportionally more recurring revenue per system

categories.name: Service & Aftermarket
ideas: Ability to offer maintenance and service contracts
Filter replacement frequency as a retention driver

categories.name: Customer Base & Channels
ideas: PM dominates Branded Stores (70%) — strong consumer brand
DM leads in Professional and DIY channels — B2B/trade focus
Channel mix affects growth strategy and margin

categories.name: Pricing & Sensitivity
ideas: DM's high unit price ($1,000 systems) may limit addressable market
PM's low unit price ($100 systems) enables mass-market scaling

categories.name: Profitability
ideas: Revenue alone does not determine which is the better investment
Need to understand cost structure and margins for each company

recommendation: Purchase PM even though its current revenue is slightly lower than DM on a per-company absolute basis (PM $4.2M vs. DM $3.3M — PM is already higher)
PM is better positioned to tap into the larger POU market through its dominant Branded Store presence and broader product range
PM's larger installed base (35,000 systems vs. 3,000) creates a stronger recurring filter revenue platform with more growth upside
risks: DM's POE business may be a maturing or declining segment as city-wide filtration infrastructure could reduce demand
Entering new market segments (e.g., POE for PM or POU for DM) requires investment and carries execution risk
PM's low unit ASP ($100) may compress margins; profitability data is needed to confirm
next_steps: Test the validity of PM entering or expanding in the POE market
Calculate potential profit with estimated market share in the POU market category
Conduct full profitability analysis (cost structure, margins) for both companies before finalizing the acquisition decision
